status: Talent now has a bounded native requisition lifecycle: a branch-scoped draft command, independent approve/reject, open/close/cancel transitions, and Company/branch/department-scoped workspace/detail reads with immutable event history, current IAM authority, versions/CAS, idempotency, audit/outbox, rollback and persisted readback. The owner also has an owner-local HTTP router and a strict Next transport with configured SSR/API cutover and fail-closed native configuration. Candidate, application, interview, proposal, offer, hire handoff, privacy and attachment workflows remain retained. The crate is not registered in the root Cargo workspace by this subagent because root Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock edits were forbidden; tests were executed in a disposable mirror workspace over the same sources.

scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified slice is the requisition lifecycle used by the Talent workspace requisition catalog and its draft/approve/reject/open/close/cancel commands. Candidate profiles and privacy, application submission and interview/select/withdraw, proposals, offers, hire handoffs, attachments, executive metrics, package obligations and every other Talent workflow remain retained TypeScript.
scope.domain: Current actor policy (selected-context expiry plus records.read, records.write and records.review), exact Company and optional branch/department scope, branch-required draft creation, bounded title/openings/target date/description/reason shapes, draft->approved/rejected/cancelled, approved->open and open->closed transitions, independent review of approve/reject, CAS expected versions, immutable event names/statuses and exact receipt/row/event projections.
scope.application: create_requisition authorizes write and current IAM before replay/source effects, validates and trims the exact draft input, rejects a missing selected branch, resolves idempotency by the command key and commits one create plan. change_requisition authorizes write and current IAM, validates the action and reason, resolves replay before the scoped locked record, rejects stale versions/wrong status/self-review and commits one CAS transition. requisition_workspace and requisition_detail validate every owner row, duplicate ids, history order and bounds before presentation.
scope.adapters: Write SQL is Talent-owned (`talent_requisitions`, `talent_requisition_events`) plus shared `command_receipts`, `audit_events` and `outbox_events`. Current assignment/principal/role authority is re-read through the existing IAM `assignments` and `iam_*` predicates already used by the retained owner. No candidate, application, proposal, offer, People, Learning, Records or Finance row is mutated. The caller's serializable Holding transaction is required; no transaction is opened, committed or retried here.
scope.http: Owner-local GET/POST /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/talent/requisitions and GET/POST /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/talent/requisitions/{requisition_id}. Exact registered Host/Holding targets and HTTPS origins, strict Idempotency-Key/Content-Type/JSON body validation, bounded bodies, unknown query rejection, private/no-store plus no-referrer/nosniff responses, and bounded BusinessError status mapping. The composition backend receives transport facts only and must supply the normal Account session, selected Company/branch/department scope, purchase admission and serializable owner unit.
scope.transport: ERPX_NATIVE_TALENT_CONFIG is strictly validated: loopback-only private base, reserved ports 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/8080 plus 5432/5433/5435 and 3200-3299 excluded, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs, 250..30000 ms timeout, bounded cookie/context/workspace headers, exact create/change bodies, exact workspace/detail/receipt shapes, Company/branch/department coherence, unique ordered rows/events and a 2 MiB response bound. A configured failure never falls back to the retained reader or command.
scope.ssr: The Talent workspace page and the feature-recruit /talent GET/POST route use native requisition rows and requisition create/change commands when ERPX_NATIVE_TALENT_CONFIG is present. An unset configuration retains talentWorkspace/createTalentRequisition/changeTalentRecord. Once configured, a malformed or failed native read/command is surfaced through the existing page/route error policy rather than silently replaced. Candidate, application, proposal, offer, privacy and handoff sections and actions remain retained.
scope.purchaseAndIdentity: The Next command cutover keeps the retained talentPurchaseControls preflight for recruit.positions and distinguishes new-work (draft, approve, open) from settle-existing (reject, close, cancel). This is a preflight, not an atomic owner unit; the composition backend must repeat current IAM, selected scope, feature release and purchase admission inside its own serializable owner transaction. The workspace merge retains the existing talentWorkspace purchased read before native requisition rows replace the catalog.
scope.crossOwnerGuards: The requisition lifecycle creates no People, Learning or Records write effect, so no such same-transaction guard is bypassed. Candidate/application slices must add their own retention, owner-eligibility and Records projection guards in the same owner transaction.
scope.notClaimed: No browser journey, authenticated page render, shared composition mount, root workspace membership, catalogue acceptance qualification, candidate/application/proposal/offer/handoff/privacy effect, job, staging, private production or Cloudflare verification.
